report.summary: Your blood report shows a few areas that need attention. Out of 14 parameters analyzed, 3 were outside the normal reference range. 1 possible deficiency indicator(s) were flagged. This report is for informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice.
critical_alerts: Wbc Count is critically low (0.15 10^3/uL) — please consult a doctor promptly.
report.doctor_consultation_reason: One or more parameters are in the critical range.

deficiencies.title: Low Vitamin B12
deficiencies.explanation: Your Vitamin B12 (12.0 ) is below the healthy reference range, which may indicate a deficiency. Needed for nerve function and red blood cell production.

health_risks.title: Wbc Count out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your Wbc Count (0.15 10^3/uL) is below the healthy reference range. White blood cells fight infection; high counts can signal infection or inflammation.

health_risks.title: Sgpt out of range
health_risks.explanation: Your Sgpt (63.55 U/L) is above the healthy reference range. A liver enzyme; elevated levels can indicate liver stress or damage.

diet_avoid: Limit ultra-processed foods and excess sugar/salt.
exercise: 150 minutes/week of moderate exercise (walking, cycling, swimming).
hydration: Drink at least 2-3 liters of water daily unless advised otherwise.
sleep: Aim for 7-8 hours of quality sleep each night, with a consistent bedtime.
stress_management: Practice 10 minutes of deep breathing, meditation, or yoga daily.
Take regular breaks from screens and prioritize downtime.
lifestyle: Get a routine annual health check-up.
Maintain a consistent sleep and wake schedule.
Include at least 30 minutes of physical activity most days of the week.

parameter_explanations.Hemoglobin: Carries oxygen in your blood. Low levels can mean anemia and cause fatigue.
parameter_explanations.Wbc Count: White blood cells fight infection; high counts can signal infection or inflammation.
parameter_explanations.Platelet Count: Platelets help your blood clot; very low or high counts need medical attention.
parameter_explanations.Fasting Blood Glucose: Blood sugar after fasting; consistently high levels can indicate prediabetes/diabetes.
parameter_explanations.Total Cholesterol: A measure of fats in your blood linked to heart disease risk.
parameter_explanations.Ldl Cholesterol: 'Bad' cholesterol — high levels raise heart disease risk.
parameter_explanations.Hdl Cholesterol: 'Good' cholesterol — higher levels help protect your heart.
parameter_explanations.Triglycerides: A type of fat in blood; high levels are linked to heart disease.
parameter_explanations.Tsh: Signals your thyroid to produce hormones; abnormal levels affect metabolism.
parameter_explanations.Vitamin D: Supports bone health and immunity; low levels are very common.
parameter_explanations.Vitamin B12: Needed for nerve function and red blood cell production.
parameter_explanations.Serum Creatinine: A waste product filtered by kidneys; high levels can signal reduced kidney function.
parameter_explanations.Sgpt: A liver enzyme; elevated levels can indicate liver stress or damage.
parameter_explanations.Calcium: Important for bones, muscles, and nerve function.
